chunk_findings.detail: The change widens the DYNAMIC program-call baseline by adding `ddflow.adapters.fs` to the allowed modules for the `DYNAMIC` family. As a result, a dynamic program call implemented in `ddflow/adapters/fs.py` (for example the `shutil.which` lookup mentioned in the new comment) is now accepted by the archifaces guard where it would previously have been rejected. This is a baseline raise for the dynamic family, contrary to the stated rule “Move the sites through their ports; never raise a baseline.” The added regression test is scoped to C6 files by its name and does not inspect this allowlist expansion, so the guard change is not caught by the new test.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/archifaces.py:63

chunk_findings.detail: The new test only asserts that the current counted program sites in the listed files are not greater than the existing baseline; it does not verify that the calls are routed through `ddflow.adapters` rather than the `ddflow.infra` compat shims. For example, if `ddflow/services/resultcache.py` is edited back to `from ..infra import git as G` while leaving the same number of counted sites, the test still passes because `n > base.get(...)` is false when the count merely returns to the old baseline value. Thus it cannot fail on the exact regression the change is meant to prevent: a listed file using the compat shim again or replacing one counted site with another while staying at or below baseline.
